subject: Day 75: dim lights after sunset
bodyText:
Today's focus
You are in the calm stretch of weeks 10-13, the right window to install systems before the 4-month shift. Today's lever is light: dimming the house after sunset reinforces the wind-down and consolidates a predictable sleep-onset routine.

Action items
- Dim every light in the house after sunset and keep the last 30 minutes before bed low and quiet, so the routine itself signals sleep. Circadian rhythm is consolidating now and external light cues are the strongest anchor you control. AAP HealthyChildren, getting baby to sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Getting-Your-Baby-to-Sleep.aspx
- Fix the order of the wind-down (feed, bath or wipe-down, lights-out song, crib) and run it the same way nightly, since predictability is what does the work, not any single step. AAP HealthyChildren, sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/default.aspx
- Confirm grandparents and any nanny are current on Tdap, flu, and COVID-19 before unsupervised contact. Pertussis is the vaccine-preventable illness most likely to kill an infant from an adult contact. AAP immunization policy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/immunizations/aap-policy-on-immunizations/
- Start a small freezer milk stash if Anoushka is returning to work, pumping one to two sessions a day. Target about 2 oz of frozen milk per missed feed.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Sleep stretches lengthening one week then shortening the next is normal variability at this age and not a setback.
- [monitor] Persistent fisted hands that rarely open, or movement that consistently favors one side; note it and raise it at the next visit.
- [call within 24h] Acute fever onset paired with a new feeding-refusal pattern, or refusal of multiple feeds in a row.
- [call now] Rectal temperature 100.4F (38.0C) or higher under 90 days, blue lips, labored breathing, or an unresponsive episode is a same-day call, and 911 for blue lips or breathing trouble!

Enrichment opportunities
- Dim the lights after sunset as the opening move of the wind-down; the dark-after-dusk cue is the most reliable sleep-onset association you can build now. AAP HealthyChildren, getting baby to sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Getting-Your-Baby-to-Sleep.aspx
- Keep one fixed lights-out song as the final step every night; the repeated, live pairing is what makes it a cue rather than background noise. Gerry et al. 2012, active music in infancy: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22490184/
- Vary tummy-time surfaces across the day toward 60 to 75 minutes cumulative, alternating a firm mat, your lap, and a slight incline to keep him pushing up on his forearms. AAP HealthyChildren, tummy to play: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 84-91: sleep consolidation window opens (~3 months); lock in the consistent sleep-wake routine before the 4-month architecture shift
- Day 112-126: 4-month well visit; vaccines RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2 (no HepB at 4 months)
- Weeks 14-18: 4-month sleep regression onset for many infants as sleep architecture matures

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at you, moves, or makes sounds to keep your attention
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Active engagement — baby is now driving the interaction, not just responding.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-to-get-attention/complete

- Pushes up on elbows during tummy time
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Tripod position. Builds toward eventual rolling.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/pushes-up-on-elbows/complete

- Holds a toy when you put it in his hand
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Voluntary grasp emerging. Soon followed by reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-toy-when-placed/complete

- Smiles on his own to get your attention
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/smiles-to-get-attention/complete

- Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/chuckles/complete
